**Label-efficient volcanic ash dispersal with conformal uncertainty** (2026)

The paper applies **conformal prediction** to the problem of volcanic ash dispersal. Conformal prediction is a framework that produces prediction sets with guaranteed coverage — meaning you can say "the ash plume is in this region with 90% confidence" without needing to assume a specific error distribution. The "label-efficient" angle suggests the method works well even when you have limited labeled training data (e.g., few satellite observations or ground-truth plume measurements), which is a common constraint in atmospheric dispersion modeling.

The abstract is brief, so the full methodological details (how the conformal sets are constructed, what data they use, how they benchmark against baselines) aren't visible to me from what's stored here. If you'd like, I can try to pull the full text to go deeper on the method and results.
